desc:
Given an array nums of non-negative integers and an integer k, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose elements add up to k or less. If no non-empty subarray qualifies, return 0.

nums = [3, 1, 2, 1, 1], k = 4
[1, 2, 1] and [2, 1, 1] both sum to 4
result = 3
hints: Checking every subarray works but is O(n²). What happens to the sum when you extend a subarray to the right?
Because nothing is negative, a longer subarray never has a smaller sum. So if a window is too heavy, only moving its left end can help.
Keep a window [left, right] and its sum. Add nums[right], then move left forward while the sum exceeds k. Record right - left + 1 after each step.
editorial: Since all values are non-negative, the window sum is non-decreasing when the right end moves right and non-increasing when the left end moves right. That monotonicity is exactly what a sliding window needs: for every right end, the valid left ends form a suffix of the possible starts, and the smallest valid left end never moves backwards as the right end advances.

Add each element to the running sum, then shrink from the left while the sum is above k. If a single element is larger than k the window becomes empty (length 0), which correctly contributes nothing. Each index enters and leaves the window at most once, so the time is O(n) with O(1) extra space.
solution:
def longestSumAtMost(nums, k):
    left = 0
    cur = 0
    best = 0
    for right, x in enumerate(nums):
        cur += x
        while cur > k:
            cur -= nums[left]
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best
